root_cause_label: Spec-Neglect Forbidden API Usage (tl.sum) and Step-Budget Exhaustion via Echo-per-Line File Writing
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent never read the task specification to discover the forbidden tl.sum API, used it repeatedly throughout its implementation, then adopted an echo-per-line file-writing strategy that exhausted the 200-step budget, culminating in a destructive file deletion at step 165 after which only a skeleton with TODO placeholders could be rebuilt.
t_err_evidence: At step 62, the agent commits to writing the solution file line-by-line using echo commands (after editors nano and vi fail), a strategy that will consume hundreds of steps on trivial file I/O instead of completing the implementation. This is the earliest decisive mistake: the agent never considered using a here-document to write the entire file at once, and this approach makes completing a correct implementation within 200 steps impossible.
t_commit_evidence: At step 77, the agent writes 'tl.sum(x_f32 * x_f32, axis=0) / N' — the first use of the explicitly forbidden tl.sum API. The agent never read the task specification (task.yaml was referenced in torch_implementation.py but never cat'd), so it has no awareness that tl.sum is prohibited. Combined with the echo-per-line strategy already consuming the step budget, the failing outcome is locked in: even if the implementation were somehow completed, the forbidden API usage would cause test failures. The agent continued using tl.sum in steps 113, 123, and 132 without any awareness or correction.
t_surface_evidence: At step 165, the agent explicitly acknowledges 'the sliding window logic is not correctly implemented' and executes 'rm triton_agent_sol.py', destroying all prior progress. This is the first visible failure signal — the agent recognizes its implementation is wrong and takes a drastic destructive action. With only 35 steps remaining after this, successful reconstruction of a complete, correct implementation is impossible.
trigger_explanation: The agent never read the task specification (task.yaml), which contains the explicit prohibition on using tl.sum (Requirement 9). The agent only read torch_implementation.py (at step 58), which mentioned task.yaml but did not reproduce the requirements. As a result, it used the forbidden tl.sum API repeatedly (steps 77, 113, 123, 132) without any awareness. Compounding this, the agent adopted an extremely inefficient echo-per-line file-writing approach (steps 62-163 and 170-200) that consumed the entire step budget without producing a complete, correct implementation.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 60-61 show 'bash: nano: command not found' and 'bash: vi: command not found', warning that the editing environment is constrained and that the echo-per-line approach adopted at step 62 would be the only fallback — a fragile strategy. Additionally, steps 6-49 show extensive idle waiting with repeated 'N/A' commands, indicating the agent was already struggling with environment management before implementation began.
